meta.title: Game Universal Reference Model
meta.numbering: L1 = domain (n), L2 = capability (n.n). Section numbers are stable identifiers and are never reused or renumbered once approved.
meta.crosswalk_rule: One section may map to many external model nodes. Repeating a field into several target models is expected, not a defect.

sections.title: Governance and Authority
sections.statement: Who may decide, who must review, and what a controlled artefact is.

sections.title: Umbrella copyright and dual-helix authority
sections.statement: Church authority and utility authority are paired under one umbrella copyright rather than a single owner.

sections.title: Church review gate
sections.statement: Doctrinal conformance and Church testing are release requirements for any parishioner-facing build.

sections.title: Controlled-document canon
sections.statement: Specifications ship as PDF with document ID, key ID, content hash, ISO-8601 stamp, watermark, copyright line and closing mark.

sections.title: Naming and mark control
sections.statement: Studio name and product title are separate assets; product titles are cleared before publication and third-party marks are never used.

sections.title: Licence posture
sections.statement: Engine and framework are permissively licensed; narrative content stays EgD-owned; every third-party asset carries a recorded licence.

sections.title: Defect register and change control
sections.statement: Breaches of canon are appended to a register in the same session, never silently corrected.

sections.title: Safety first, betterment second
sections.statement: Where safety and capability conflict, safety wins and the trade is recorded.

sections.title: Safeguarding and Child Protection
sections.statement: The walls around a child-facing surface, stated before any feature.

sections.title: Closed communication walls
sections.statement: No chat, voice channels, friend requests, camera, microphone, uploads, advertising, trackers or outbound links on the child surface.

sections.title: Describe before generate
sections.statement: The child must describe intent in their own words before any generative step runs.

sections.title: Mandatory Stand-Up
sections.statement: Every twelve minutes of active play triggers a non-skippable 66-second eyes, spine and reach break with a seated accommodation. The interval may be shortened for younger cohorts, never lengthened.

sections.title: Fictional-imagery notice
sections.statement: Imaginative or symbolic imagery is labelled as fiction at the point of display.

sections.title: Age banding and cohort scope
sections.statement: Content, session length and social surface are bounded by age band and school cohort.

sections.title: Consent and skip gates
sections.statement: Start position, consent and skip gates run before the guided demo; interaction unlocks only in the play phase.

sections.title: Guardian visibility
sections.statement: A guardian can see what the child saw without surveilling the child in real time.

sections.title: Narrative Canon and Provenance
sections.statement: What the story is allowed to assert, and on whose authority.

sections.title: Claim classification
sections.statement: Every narrative claim is tagged record, inference, lore, or author framing. Untagged claims do not ship.

sections.title: Source-tagged corpus
sections.statement: Narrative source material carries citations to primary sources and records its own corrections.

sections.title: Bounded Enoch adaptation
sections.statement: Only the Astronomical Book, 1 Enoch 72-82, is adapted, for calendar and heritage mechanics. Judgment and Watchers material is excluded from the main path.

sections.title: Heritage chapter line
sections.statement: Acadian survival-and-rebuild chapters use the defensible 1636-1650 Port-Royal arrival range and make no oldest-site claim.

sections.title: Narrator character bench
sections.statement: Uriel is the child-facing companion. Penemue is reserved for a truth-ledger lane. Valentinian Sophia is excluded in favour of Proverbs-Wisdom.

sections.title: Copyright-limited corpus handling
sections.statement: Public-domain texts are stored in full; copyrighted editions are represented bibliographically only.

sections.title: Worldbuilding boundary
sections.statement: Ideal-world and double-sphere imagery is framed as imagination, never as a prescriptive real-world claim.

sections.title: Convergence labelling
sections.statement: Overlaps between sources are marked direct, structural or speculative, and non-convergences are recorded too.

sections.title: Learning Design
sections.statement: The teaching model the game exists to carry.

sections.title: Education parent, religion subsection
sections.statement: The parent programme is education; religious education is one part of it.

sections.title: Fixed-output catechetical path
sections.statement: Catechetical answers are reviewed and deterministic, never open-ended generation.

sections.title: Lesson primitives
sections.statement: Circle, triangle and sphere are the base geometric lesson objects the mechanics build on.

sections.title: Chapter and progression model
sections.statement: Content is delivered as numbered chapters with an explicit unlock rule.

sections.title: Service-and-evidence credibility
sections.statement: Standing is earned through evidenced help to others, not follower counts, streaks or engagement.

sections.title: Assessment and mastery evidence
sections.statement: Progress is evidenced by artefacts the learner produced, not time on task.

sections.title: Game as doorway
sections.statement: The game lowers the entry barrier; education, the twin and free choice remain the process it carries.

sections.title: Identity and Digital Twin
sections.statement: Who the player is to the system, and what the system owes them.

sections.title: Starter-twin quest
sections.statement: Onboarding is request access, authenticate, fork a starter twin, connect everyday tools.

sections.title: Three doors
sections.statement: Humans enter as Mother, Child or Father; institutions are sorted separately as electric utility, other utility, or enterprise.

sections.title: Consent-first protection message
sections.statement: The first cross-cultural message is protection, not capability.

sections.title: Soft identification tier
sections.statement: Adult surfaces let the reader start freely and ask for identity only after meaningful engagement.

sections.title: Twin ownership and portability
sections.statement: The twin's data belongs to the person and can be exported without permission from the platform.

sections.title: Authentication backend
sections.statement: Identity verification runs through a named backend rather than hard-coded logic.

sections.title: World and Level Structure
sections.statement: How space is described so every chapter is built the same way.

sections.title: Scene graph contract
sections.statement: One scene per chapter, one root per scene, no cross-scene node paths.

sections.title: Metric ground plane
sections.statement: Units are metres. The floor's top surface sits at y = 0 and a character's origin is at its feet.

sections.title: Chapter world inventory
sections.statement: Each chapter declares its geometry, interactables, spawn points and exits as data before it is built.

sections.title: The Village
sections.statement: A shared, voice-first common surface bounded by the child's school or cohort, with no feed-style global discovery.

sections.title: Navigation and blocking volumes
sections.statement: Walkable area and blocked area are authored explicitly, not inferred from visual geometry.

sections.title: Browser scene budget
sections.statement: Visible polygon count stays under roughly 50,000 and textures under 1024 px for the browser lane.

sections.title: Interaction and Control
sections.statement: The contract between the player's hands and the world.

sections.title: Named input actions
sections.statement: Code binds to named actions such as move_forward, never to raw key codes. This buys gamepad support and rebinding for free.

sections.title: Camera-relative movement
sections.statement: Forward means away from the camera. Input is rotated by the camera rig's basis before it becomes velocity.

sections.title: Split camera rig
sections.statement: Yaw lives on a rig node, pitch lives on a spring arm, so rotations cannot interfere and the camera cannot roll or clip walls.

sections.title: Feel constants as contract
sections.statement: SPEED, ACCEL and TURN_SPEED are published tunables. Defaults are 5.5 m/s, 60, and 12.

sections.title: Voice-first village interaction
sections.statement: Movement and voice are the primary interaction metaphor in the common surface, not text entry.

sections.title: Touch and gamepad parity
sections.statement: Every action reachable by keyboard is reachable by touch and by gamepad.

sections.title: Simulation and Rules
sections.statement: What the world does when nobody is pressing anything.

sections.title: Fixed-tick simulation
sections.statement: Game logic advances on a fixed physics tick independent of frame rate.

sections.title: Sequenced actions
sections.statement: Multi-frame actions such as a sword swing, a cutscene or a boss phase are written as coroutines, not state-machine sprawl.

sections.title: Interaction volumes and timed windows
sections.statement: Hits and triggers use explicit volumes enabled for an explicit number of frames.

sections.title: Deterministic puzzle state
sections.statement: Puzzle outcomes are reproducible from recorded input; no hidden randomness in assessed content.

sections.title: Lossy-save assumption
sections.statement: Browser storage is assumed to be unreliable. Progress that matters is recoverable from the server or re-earnable.

sections.title: Presentation and Audio
sections.statement: How it looks and sounds, bounded by the delivery target.

sections.title: Renderer profile
sections.statement: Browser lane runs WebGL 2.0 with a compatibility-class renderer. Advanced deferred rendering is native-lane only.

sections.title: Lighting and tonemap profile
sections.statement: One directional key light with shadows, AgX tonemapping, ambient contribution from sky.

sections.title: Palette and typography canon
sections.statement: Cream #fdfaf4, cream-2 #f7f2e7, ink #1a1a1a, line #e7e1d3, mute #6b665c, accent orange #e87722. Fraunces display, Inter body.

sections.title: UI shell and HUD
sections.statement: Chrome is minimal during play; the safety timer and chapter title are the only persistent elements.

sections.title: Audio ceiling
sections.statement: No more than eight to ten simultaneous audio streams in the browser lane; fewer on mobile.

sections.title: Asset Pipeline and Open Standards
sections.statement: The interchange contract. This is the layer that makes the work portable.

sections.title: glTF 2.0 as the interchange format
sections.statement: Every 3D asset and scene crosses tool boundaries as glTF 2.0, binary .glb preferred. This is the published ISO standard and the lowest common denominator across engines.

sections.title: Texture container
sections.statement: Textures ship as KTX2 with Basis Universal supercompression where the runtime supports it, PNG otherwise.

sections.title: Resolution and budget ceiling
sections.statement: 1024 px texture ceiling for the browser lane; 2048 permitted native.

sections.title: Naming and folder convention
sections.statement: Assets are named by chapter and role, not by author or date.

sections.title: Asset provenance register
sections.statement: Every imported asset records source URL, licence, and pinned commit or version.

sections.title: Authoring toolchain
sections.statement: Blender for modelling, an open engine for scene assembly, both exporting glTF. No proprietary interchange format in the chain.

sections.title: Platform, Build and Delivery
sections.statement: How it becomes a URL.

sections.title: Browser baseline
sections.statement: The delivery target is a modern browser with WebAssembly and WebGL 2.0. No installer, no store, no plugin.

sections.title: Two-lane engine strategy
sections.statement: A WebGL-2 web runtime is the public lane; a full desktop engine is the authoring and native lane. glTF is the seam between them, so neither lane owns the content.

sections.title: Hosting profile
sections.statement: GitHub Pages by default. Cross-origin isolation headers are required only if the runtime uses shared-memory threading.

sections.title: Reproducible build
sections.statement: Build artefacts are produced by a committed script from a pinned toolchain, never by hand.

sections.title: Public URL as deliverable
sections.statement: Work exists when it is committed, pushed, and fetched successfully from its public URL.

sections.title: Data, Telemetry and Privacy
sections.statement: What is recorded, and what is deliberately not.

sections.title: No trackers on the child surface
sections.statement: No analytics, advertising identifiers or third-party beacons on any child-facing page.

sections.title: Local-first state
sections.statement: Play state stays on the device unless the player chooses to sync it.

sections.title: Adult review-signal logging
sections.statement: Engagement and review signals are logged on adult outreach surfaces only, and disclosed there.

sections.title: Retention and deletion
sections.statement: Every stored field has a stated retention period and a working deletion path.

sections.title: Witnessed, not surveilled
sections.statement: Visibility to a trusted adult is the privacy metaphor; continuous monitoring is not.

sections.title: Integration and Interoperability
sections.statement: How this model plugs into everything else you own.

sections.title: Knowledge-graph surface
sections.statement: Narrative, lesson and progress entities are exposed as a temporal knowledge graph rather than locked in the build.

sections.title: Agent-tool surface
sections.statement: The graph is exposed over a standard agent-tool protocol so external assistants can read it.

sections.title: Portal embedding
sections.statement: The playable embeds inside the parish or institution portal rather than living as a standalone secular surface.

sections.title: Crosswalk registry
sections.statement: Every section number here carries a crosswalk row to external reference models. Repeating one field into many target models is expected and permitted.

sections.title: Lowest-denominator rule
sections.statement: Where two external models disagree, this model holds the simpler shape and maps upward, never downward.

sections.title: Operations and Lifecycle
sections.statement: Keeping it alive and affordable.

sections.title: Repository as the record
sections.statement: The session is a scratchpad. Anything that matters is recoverable by cloning the repository and nothing else.

sections.title: Release gates
sections.statement: Church review, safety review, accessibility check and a fetched public URL all pass before a release is called done.

sections.title: Self-healing log
sections.statement: Decisions and corrections are captured as committed log entries, not left in chat.

sections.title: Cost control
sections.statement: Spend is measured against a declared daily control before expensive work is authorised.

sections.title: Peer-review intake
sections.statement: A public front door collects parent and peer feedback and routes it to a named channel.

sections.title: Accessibility and Localisation
sections.statement: Who can actually play it.

sections.title: Contrast and focus
sections.statement: Text and interactive elements meet published contrast and keyboard-focus guidance.

sections.title: Seated accommodation
sections.statement: Every physical prompt, including the Stand-Up, has a seated equivalent.

sections.title: Language set
sections.statement: English, French and Spanish are first-class. Strings are externalised, never embedded in scenes.

sections.title: Low-end device profile
sections.statement: A named minimum device and connection profile is tested each release.

sections.title: Reading-level control
sections.statement: Child-facing text is held to a stated reading level and checked, not assumed.
